**Continuous 2.38.10**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.38.9, 2.38.8, 2.38.7, 2.38.6, 2.38.5, 2.38.4, 2.38.3, 2.38.2, 2.38.1, 2.38.0, 2.36.0, 2.34.0, 2.32.0, 2.30.0, 2.28.0, 2.26.0, 2.24.0, 2.22.0, 2.20.0, 2.18.0, 2.16.3, 2.16.2, 2.16.1, 2.16.0, 2.14.0, 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.38.10.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                         |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.38.10.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.38.10.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.38.10.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.38.10.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.38.10.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.38.10.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.38.10-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.38.10.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.38.10-vscode/continuous-cli-2.38.10.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). The short command `cn` also works; both run the same program. It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.38.9

Checks that stop commands no longer run unless you turn them on, and the checks that remain no longer read the inside of a quoted script as shell. The agent is also told when it repeats itself, instead of being invited to.

### New

- **The active config is named everywhere you change something.** A config can mix providers and models, so which one is active decides what the Models, MCP servers, Tools, Permissions and Rules tabs edit. Every Settings tab now starts with "Active config: Bedrock bedrock.yaml" and a Switch link to the Configs tab. The Configs tab marks the active row with an "Active" badge and a bar down its side, where it used to say a small "selected". The model picker's list shows the config its models come from beside "Models".
- **The agent is told when it repeats a call.** If it sends a command, or a small rewrite of one, that was refused, the second refusal says so and names other ways to go on. If it runs the same command three times in a row and gets the same result, the result says "You just ran that same command 3 times" and suggests another approach: read what the output says, write the script to a file with `create_new_file` and run that, split the work up, look with `read_file`, `grep_search` or `ls`, or tell you what is in the way. Nothing is stopped. The note is part of the result the model reads, not only a label on the card. The switch is "Tell the agent when it repeats a call", in Settings > Permissions > Protections, and it is on unless you turn it off. No preset changes it.

### Behaviour changes

- **"Check shell commands before running them" is off unless you turn it on.** It is in Settings > Permissions > Protections. On, it stops a command the shell would reject before it runs: bash in PowerShell (`export`, heredocs, `&&` in Windows PowerShell 5.1), PowerShell in bash, an inline script that quoting breaks, and a program that is not installed. Off, the command runs as written and the shell reports any error. In 2.38.9 it was on until switched off, and IDGAF did not turn it off; no preset touches it now.
- **A likely mistake no longer stops a command once.** The shell check used to stop a command that "often goes wrong", then let the identical command through the second time. That taught the model that sending it again works, and a model that rewrites a command a little never sends the identical text, so it looped. Only a mistake that is certain stops a call now, and its message says that sending the same command again is refused the same way.
- **The protections list counts only the rules a preset sets.** "11 of 11 on" is unchanged; the two rules you own are named beside it when they are not at their defaults.

### Fixes

- **A quoted script is data, not shell.** The command check read the text inside strings, here-strings and heredoc bodies as shell. A multi-line `python -c "..."` with a line like `total=len(x) + 1` was refused as "NAME=value command is bash"; an `export` line, `2>/dev/null` or a `<<` inside a quoted script, or a PowerShell-looking line in a heredoc body, was flagged too. Those commands were valid. The check now reads only what the shell reads as code, and it still finds a bare `&&`, a bash heredoc, `export` and `NAME=value` outside any string.
- **Commands stopped under IDGAF.** `&&`, heredocs and inline scripts in Windows PowerShell 5.1 were refused even at IDGAF, by the engine and by the terminal tool's own check. Neither runs unless the shell switch is on.
